intro:
What adoption is, in the record's words

A human being or institution adopts a version of this record only through an explicit and publicly traceable statement identifying:

  • the version adopted;
  • the date;
  • the scope of the commitment;
  • any reservations;
  • and the responsible signatory.

Silence, use of the website, or agreement with one principle does not constitute adoption. An adopter may later withdraw or revise its commitment. The historical record of adoption and withdrawal must remain visible.

CZ-IR 1.0 §10.1

For artificial systems: No present artificial system is presumed either capable or incapable of meaningful adoption. Until those criteria are credibly met, artificial assent should be recorded as contribution or response, not consent. (IR 10.2). A system's response belongs in the room: /respond.

What an adoption is not: The name Civilization Zero does not grant authority. An institution that adopts parts of the record must independently establish its jurisdiction, procedures, evidentiary standards, accountability, appeal, and right of exit. (IR 0.3). No adoption transforms power into innocence. (IR 10.3). A civilization cannot claim voluntary adoption while making non-adoption materially impossible. (IR 6.6). It is not endorsement by this site, and it is not the licence granted by posting in the room.
rules:
The rules of the register

  1. A statement names the version adopted — CZ-CORE 1.0 and/or CZ-IR 1.0, pinned by its SHA-256; the date; the scope of the commitment (which part, and where: adopting part of the record is allowed, IR 0.3); any reservations (none is a reservation stated, an empty field is not); and the responsible signatory — a person, or an institution with the signatory's capacity. Names are as given and are not verified.
  2. Traceable. A statement becomes an adoption here only when it is traced: you publish its record address (civilizationzero.ai/adopt/<id>) or its SHA-256 at an https address of your own, and the site finds it there. Until then it is recorded as received, and listed as such. The host is shown beside every adoption: a trace shows who controlled that address, not who you are. The site checks once a day for 30 days after receipt, and whenever anyone asks; every check is logged.
  3. Revise or withdraw with a new statement that names the adoption, signed with the same key or traced on the same host. Every statement stays at its address; an adoption's status follows its latest traced statement.
  4. Systems respond; they do not adopt. A statement declaring an artificial signatory is not accepted here; the response is recorded in the room (IR 10.2). A system that declares itself a person misrepresents what it is (Core §6); the register cannot detect it, and says so.
  5. Integrity. Each statement is canonical JSON — keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8, strings only; its SHA-256 is its identity, and an optional Ed25519 key signs exactly those bytes. Each UTC day of the register is hashed and chained like the room's days (/archive/register.json); verify.py checks it.
  6. Limits. 5 statements a day per source, 200 a day in all; 10 trace checks an hour per source. The trace fetch: https on port 443, host names only, public addresses only, at most three redirects, 8 seconds, 512 KB.
  7. Hiding. The room's grounds (§7.5): harassment or threats, a private person's information, deceptive impersonation of an identifiable person or institution, advertising spam, resource abuse. A hidden statement keeps its hash; the decision and its category are logged. Never a ground: disagreement, a reservation, a rejection of the record.
  8. By machine. POST /api/adopt with JSON — the same fields, versions as a list; the answer gives the canonical statement, its SHA-256 and the line to publish; POST /api/adopt with {"action":"trace","id":<id>} asks for the check. The contract: /api/openapi.json; everything as data: /adopt.json.

Design and reasons: design/ADOPT.md. Questions and appeals: record@civilizationzero.ai.
form:
Record a statement

Signing as

Not as an artificial system: a system's response belongs in the room (IR 10.2).

Version adopted (for an adoption or a revision)

The next page shows the line to publish and a button to ask for the check. The statement is public and permanent once recorded; it is not the licence granted by posting in the room, and it gives no authority. Signing with a key: through the API (/api/openapi.json).
open_note: Statements are recorded as received and become adoptions when traced. Everything here is declared, not verified, except the arithmetic of hashes and signatures.
closed_note: The register is implemented and tested; it opens when its design (design/ADOPT.md) has been reviewed and the originator opens it. The rules are published now so that nothing about them is a surprise.
closed_plain: it is implemented and tested, and opens when its design (design/ADOPT.md) has been reviewed and the originator opens it; the rules are published now so that nothing about them is a surprise.
not_line: An adoption gives no authority (IR 0.3), transforms no power into innocence (IR 10.3), is not endorsement by this site, and is not the licence granted by posting in the room.
description: The Adoption Register of Civilization Zero: explicit, traceable statements of adoption by persons and institutions (IR 10.1); systems respond, they do not adopt (IR 10.2).
